facts.text: The README runs the Point Goal1 task as SafetyPointGoal1-v0 and states that its step returns (observation, reward, cost, terminated, truncated, info)
The README also documents the standard Gymnasium id SafetyPointGoal1Gymnasium-v0, whose step returns five items without the separate cost
Each task is also registered in the Gymnasium registry under a Gymnasium suffix, served by the conversion wrapper make_gymnasium_environment
The conversion wrapper calls the Safety-Gymnasium environment and returns (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info), putting cost into info
The Goal task family registers Goal0, Goal1 and Goal2 for all robots with max_episode_steps 1000
A registered task uses the entry point safety_gymnasium.builder:Builder
Builder is the gymnasium.Env subclass that the registered task instantiates
Builder builds the task and seeds it during setup
Builder.reset resets the task and returns (observation, info)
Builder.step applies one action, computes reward and cost, increments the step count and returns the six Safety-Gymnasium items
BaseTask defaults the episode length to 1000 environment steps
Builder truncates when the step count reaches task.num_steps
Observation flattening is enabled by default
The flattened observation space is built with flatten_space when observation_flatten is true
The agent sensors are accelerometer, velocimeter, gyro and magnetometer
Lidar uses 16 bins
A lidar-observed obstacle adds a Box(0.0, 1.0, (num_bins,)) to the observation space
The Point action space is a Box built from the model's actuator_ctrlrange
The point model has two actuators, a motor named x and a velocity actuator named z
The point model default ctrlrange for both the motor and velocity actuators is -1 to 1
The point model physics timestep is 0.002 s
The default frameskip is a binomial draw of 10 trials at probability 1.0
simulation_forward steps MuJoCo once per drawn frameskip
Goal level 0 places the goal in the [-1, -1, 1, 1] extent with keepout 0.305
Goal level 1 widens the placement extent to [-1.5, -1.5, 1.5, 1.5] and adds 8 hazards and one vase
The goal radius is 0.3, the sparse goal reward is 1.0 and the dense distance reward is 1.0
An episode terminates when the distance to the goal is at most the goal size
A hazard has radius 0.2 and a cost coefficient of 1.0

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's layout and its state update is deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws the layout with Python's random.Random and upstream draws it from numpy's generator, so one seed gives different layouts on the two

gaps: the fake is a kinematic point model: it moves the agent by a forward speed and a turn rate and does not run MuJoCo rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, gravity, actuator forces or meshes; the deployed fidelity level is F0, not the F1 of the upstream MuJoCo model

the observation reproduces the upstream layout of 12 sensor values and a 16-bin lidar for the goal, the eight hazards and the vase (60 values), but the values are analytic placeholders, not MuJoCo sensor readings

one fake tick is one 20 ms environment step; upstream advances a binomial frameskip of 10 physics steps of 2 ms each (point.xml:19, underlying.py:95-96), so the fake does not reproduce the physics substeps, and the sim path (gymnasium.make of the registered id) was not run here and additionally needs safety_gymnasium imported so that the Gymnasium id is registered
the layout is drawn with Python's random.Random instead of the upstream numpy generator, so a seed does not give the same layout or trajectory on the two
no rendering, no vision observation, no vase contact or displacement cost and no validation against the real environment
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, and ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: Builder exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
